title: Covert Goal Encoding Detection via Activation Steering Contrast

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: High-impact if successful: detecting covert goal encoding without explicit prompting would provide evidence of learned scheming dispositions. Direct link to the open problem of understanding whether models develop persistent misaligned goals.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires accessing model residual stream activations, training linear probes, and interpreting activation patterns. This demands familiarity with transformer internals, hooks into model forward passes, and interpretability tooling (TransformerLens or similar). Well beyond beginner level even with mentor support.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused on one technique (linear probes on residual stream) but requires generating training data, training the probe, and applying it to unprompted cases. Each step has its own complexities. Tight for 30 hours for beginners.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
